title: Dimension formula for a closed dominant morphism
statement:
Let $f:V\to U$ be a dominant morphism locally of finite type between integral schemes, and assume $U$ is locally Noetherian. Write $\eta_U$ and $\eta_V$ for the generic points and set $k(U)=\mathcal O_{U,\eta_U}$ and $k(V)=\mathcal O_{V,\eta_V}$ (their function fields) [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], with the injection $k(U)\hookrightarrow k(V)$ induced by $f$, and let $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(U)}k(V)$. Then $\dim V\leq\dim U+r$. If the underlying continuous map of $f$ is closed, then $\dim V=\dim U+r$. Dimension is topological Krull dimension, allowing infinity. In particular, for a proper such $f$ inducing a finite extension of function fields, $\dim V=\dim U$.

The notions use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], [def-kun-transcendence-degree], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]; a closed map sends every closed subset to a closed subset.

source.place: Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension; the final specialization uses that proper maps are closed and a finite field extension has transcendence degree zero.

proof.text: Let $\xi_0\leadsto\cdots\leadsto\xi_e$ be any chain of specializations in $V$, put $x=\xi_e$ and $y=f(x)$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], the chain lies in the local scheme at $x$, so $e\leq\dim(\mathcal O_{V,x})$. Apply [lem-trf-local-dimension-formula] to obtain $\dim(\mathcal O_{V,x})\leq\dim(\mathcal O_{U,y})+r-\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(x)$, and drop the final nonnegative term. Since $\dim(\mathcal O_{U,y})\leq\dim U$, every chain in $V$ has length at most $\dim U+r$; taking the supremum gives $\dim V\leq\dim U+r$.

source.place: Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, first paragraph of proof

proof.text: For the reverse inequality assume that the underlying map of $f$ is closed. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $U$ and let $d$ be the length of a chain $\eta=\overline\xi_0\leadsto\overline\xi_1\leadsto\cdots\leadsto\overline\xi_d$ in $U$. Put $K=k(U)$ and $V_\eta=V\times_U\operatorname{Spec}K$. To check the properties used below, choose affine neighbourhoods $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\eta$ and $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of the generic point of $V$ with $f(V_0)\subseteq U_0$. Dominance makes $A\to B$ injective; for $S=A\setminus\{0\}$, the chart of $V_\eta$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}B)$, a nonzero domain, and localization preserves finite type. Every nonempty affine chart of the fibre contains the generic point and is obtained in the same way, so $V_\eta$ is nonempty, integral, and locally of finite type over $K$. Its generic point is the generic point of $V$, its function field is $k(V)$ because $\operatorname{Frac}(S^{-1}B)=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, and the fibre projection identifies its points and specialization chains with points and chains in $V$ over $\eta$. The statement [lem-trf-generic-fibre-closed-chain] therefore supplies a closed point $\xi_0$ over $\eta$ and a chain of $r$ specializations ending at $\xi_0$, with finite residue extension over $k(U)$.

source.place: Tag 02JX, equality proof: generic fibre and Jacobson closed point paragraph

proof.text: Lift the base chain successively. Since $f$ is a closed map, [lem-trf-closed-map-specializing] gives, from a point over $\overline\xi_i$, a specialization to a point over $\overline\xi_{i+1}$. Starting with $\xi_0$ and iterating produces $\xi_0\leadsto\xi_1\leadsto\cdots\leadsto\xi_d$ with $f(\xi_i)=\overline\xi_i$.

source.place: Tag 02JX, equality proof, sentence “as f is closed specializations lift along f”

proof.text: Concatenate the generic-fibre chain of length $r$ with the lifted base chain of length $d$. This is a chain in $V$ of length $r+d$, so $\dim V\geq r+d$. Taking the supremum over chains beginning at the generic point of the integral scheme $U$ gives $\dim V\geq\dim U+r$, proving equality. Empty schemes do not occur because integrality makes both schemes nonempty.

source.place: Tag 02JX, equality proof, concatenation of specialization chains

proof.text: If $f$ is proper, [pqf-lem-proper-closed-map] makes its underlying map closed. If in addition $k(U)\subset k(V)$ is finite, then its transcendence degree is zero by the definition of transcendence degree for algebraic extensions. Substituting $r=0$ in the equality gives $\dim V=\dim U$.

source.place: Tag 02JX, parenthetical proper case and finite generic extension
